title: Slatelet: telemetry-driven admin microcommands + atomic runbook bundler
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Oncall and support engineers repeatedly reach for small, composable admin commands to perform scoped remediation (rotate a key, clear a cache shard, resubmit a job). Current runbook execution is heavyweight and often requires copying steps across tickets, which increases time-to-repair and audit surface.

Goal: Build a lightweight admin microcommand framework ("slatelets") that: (1) exposes safe, parameterized admin primitives as one-line CLI commands and HTTP endpoints; (2) automatically attaches structured telemetry and provenance for every invocation; and (3) provides a bundler that compiles a sequence of slatelets into an atomic, idempotent runbook task that can be scheduled, dry-run, or audited.

Acceptance criteria:
- Slatelet CLI prototype with 8 core primitives (cache:invalidate, job:resubmit, model:rollforward, token:revoke, route:drain, capacity:drain, quota:adjust, incident:annotate) implemented and documented.
- Each slatelet emits structured telemetry (event id, caller, params, input-hash, pre/post snapshot reference) and stores provenance to the admin-events index.
- Bundler accepts a YAML list of slatelets and produces a single task artifact with clear rollback hooks, idempotency checks, and dry-run mode.
- RBAC checks enforced via console permission surface and CLI flags; unauthorized attempts are rejected with audit entry.
- End-to-end test coverage (unit + integration) for slatelet execution, bundler compile/dry-run, and two-stage canary rollout in staging.

Technical approach:
1) Design slatelet RPC/CLI contract: small JSON input, explicit outputs, and optional sidecar snapshots. Keep stdout/stderr semantics simple to parse.
2) Implement server-side slatelet shim that wraps existing admin helpers (existing runbook snippets) and ensures structured telemetry is emitted via trace/metric + admin-events Kafka topic.
3) Build bundler service that compiles YAML -> task manifest, injects idempotency tokens, and attaches rollback scripts. The manifest is JSONL-friendly for run queue ingestion.
4) Safety: dry-run mode, automatic prechecks (quota/capacity/lock), per-slatelet timeouts, and an emergency abort with guaranteed rollback for supported primitives.
5) Observability: dashboard in Console showing slatelet runs, latencies, failures, and provenance link to ticket/PR.

Out-of-scope for MVP: cross-account private deploys, full orchestration UI (we will integrate with rollouts later).
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: aligned with PM and SRE. PM wants first-class audit trail for execs; SRE emphasized per-slatelet timeouts and prechecks.

2026-03-04 - Design review: split CLI vs HTTP invocation paths; decided to keep a single service with two adapters to avoid duplication. See design note: https://confluence.internal/redwood/slatelets-design.

2026-03-06 - Spike complete: implemented prototype for cache:invalidate and job:resubmit on dev cluster. Prototype emits admin-events to Kafka (topic: admin-events). Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/slatelets/pull/12.

2026-03-09 - Security sync: RBAC model reviewed with Security. Need permission 'slatelet.execute' plus per-primitive allow-list. Security review required for model:rollforward. Added to security_review_required.

2026-03-11 - Integration test: bundler successfully compiled a 3-step YAML into a task manifest and passed dry-run assertions on staging. Next: wire console dashboard and schedule canary run for 2026-03-15. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/slatelets/pull/34.
2026-03-11 - Blockers: depend on ENG-314159 for runbook-typed-api to accept JSONL manifests; dependency tracked.
